title: The Tax Collector Now Gets a Cut of What He Finds - Whatfinger News Quick Hits
text:
Arguably the most famous man on the planet throughout the 1700s was the famed writer François-Marie Arouet, known to history as Voltaire. He wasn’t just a celebrity writer and philosopher, however; Voltaire was also a wealthy capitalist and nobleman who almost single-handedly turned the impoverished region of Ferney into a highly productive watchmaking hub.
Through his fame and creativity, Voltaire managed to attract a small army of Swiss watchmakers to relocate across the border into France and set up shop in Ferney. As part of the deal, he personally negotiated special tax incentives for his watchmakers, exempting them from some of the most onerous French national taxes.
